sections.h2: Who does what with a tax bill
sections.html:
Four county offices share the job. The PVA, at (270) 343-4395, assigns each parcel its worth. The sheriff, at (270) 343-2191, takes the money. The clerk, at (270) 343-2125, picks up bills nobody paid in time. The county attorney, at (270) 343-2121, mails the warning letters that come before the clerk's sale of delinquent bills.

A complaint about the number belongs with the PVA, while a question about where to send a check belongs with the sheriff.

sections.h2: Russell County for a home seller
sections.html:
Jamestown holds the courthouse, and Russell Springs is the larger town at 2,715 residents in 2020. The whole county counts as rural. Lake Cumberland and the Cumberland Parkway draw buyers, and the lake's drawdown years from 2007 to 2014 still prompt questions from lakefront buyers. Clocks here run on Central time while neighboring counties to the east run on Eastern, so confirm the hour when a distant buyer or title office schedules your closing.

Homes are modest in price and the stock is loose. The July 2025 estimate is 18,608 people, up from 17,991 in April 2020. There are 7,562 households, and owners live in 70.8 percent of homes. A typical owner-occupied value is $163,200, typical gross rent is $681, and owner costs with a mortgage run $1,219 a month. Median household income is $44,738. The 2020 count listed 10,088 housing units, with 26.0 percent vacant. Only 5 building permits were issued in 2025, so you are not competing with new builds.

Seasonal cabins, inherited houses and homes several years behind on tax deserve a written payoff from the clerk before you list. Lakefront sellers can also ask the county surveyor for help when a shoreline line is in doubt.

Kentucky's statutory calendar, KRS 134.015, governs here. Mail arrives in October, and the sheriff stays open for payment right up to April 15 of the next year.

Russell County: charge by payment date
Payment dateWhat you owe
On or before November 1Printed bill minus 2 percent
November 2 through December 31Printed amount, no change
JanuaryPrinted amount plus 5 percent
February 1 onwardPrinted amount plus 10 percent
After April 15Clerk handles the unpaid bill

The law makes the January 1 owner personally liable, so spell out in your sales contract who repays whom.

sections.h2: What happens if a bill is still open on April 15?
sections.html:
Your sheriff hands it off to the clerk, who turns it into a certificate of delinquency with a lien recorded on the parcel. New owners inherit that lien. The clerk commits to a sale before August ends, advertised in the paper and online. Private buyers who register with the state may buy the certificate and then chase the owner for payment.

  • Amounts on the clerk's delinquent list move monthly, so ask for a fresh payoff figure.
  • Interest of 1 percent per month runs on the certificate, with clerk and attorney commissions on top.
  • A title search will surface the lien, so settle it ahead of closing.

Begin with an informal talk at the PVA; a phone call counts. When that goes nowhere, a written petition goes to the clerk no later than the workday following the end of roll inspection. Bring listings, building costs or loan papers. The appeal does not freeze collection, so pay on your own claimed figure while it runs.

Two groups qualify: owners 65 and over, and owners classified as totally disabled. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the state's deduction is $49,100. About 22.6 percent of residents are past 65, so many local owners will want it.

Apply at the PVA. Anyone claiming disability needs a federal or retirement-system classification, and most renew each year. The state changes the dollar amount now and then, so confirm this year's figure.

sections.h2: What changes at the closing table
sections.html:
Closing agents usually pull the current bill and any delinquent payoff, so ask for both early. A bill open before April 15 sits with the sheriff, and after that date it sits with the clerk, plus extra charges.

A buyer who spots a lien in the title search will demand its removal or leave. Pair your listing with a clean paper trail: a current bill, a payoff letter if needed, and a plain answer on any back years. Several unpaid years on an inherited house can eat most of the equity, which is the situation where a direct cash sale appeals to owners who want the debt paid at closing without making repairs first.

sections.h2: A year in the life of a bill
sections.html:
Knowing the sequence helps you decide when to list. October brings the mailbox surprise. If you pay everything by November 1, you keep 2 percent. December 31 is the plain deadline. Wait until January and 5 percent lands on top, and from February 1 it becomes 10 percent. April 15 ends the sheriff's turn.

After that the bill moves to the clerk, interest begins at 1 percent monthly, and the sale comes before August is out. A seller who closes in spring should assume the prior year's bill is still in their name, even if the contract says the buyer reimburses part of it.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with a tax bill
sections.html:
Whatever your situation, this order keeps things tidy.

  1. Phone the sheriff, (270) 343-2191, and find out if this year's bill shows paid.
  2. An older year still open? The clerk, (270) 343-2125, quotes a payoff with interest and fees folded in.
  3. While the house is still yours, ask the PVA, (270) 343-4395, if you qualify for the homestead deduction.
  4. Disclose each open amount to the closing agent before anyone signs.
  5. Reconfirm the payoff a few days ahead, because delinquent amounts move monthly, and bring a photo ID and your deed to the closing office.

Sellers with a lakefront cabin that sits empty much of the year often miss mail. Give the sheriff a current mailing address so bills and county attorney letters actually reach you.

sections.h2: Selling for cash when taxes are behind
sections.html: A direct cash buyer does not need a bank to approve the house, so a lien or old tax debt does not stall the deal the way it can with a mortgage buyer. The title company still finds the lien. The payoff is simply taken from your sale money when papers are signed, and you leave with the rest. For an inherited house with several years unpaid, that route can end the problem in one meeting. Ask the title company to show the payoff line on your settlement statement so you can see exactly what was paid and to whom.

faqs.q: Where does a Russell County tax payment go?
faqs.a: The sheriff's office takes it, (270) 343-2191, until April 15 of the following year. Past that date the county clerk, (270) 343-2125, holds unpaid bills.

faqs.q: What does a late Russell County payment cost?
faqs.a: January adds five percent, and ten percent applies from February 1. When the bill reaches the clerk, interest of 1 percent a month starts, plus clerk and county attorney fees.

faqs.q: Will a Russell County tax lien follow a house into a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays on the parcel until the tax is paid or the 11-year limit in KRS 134.420 runs out, no matter who owns it. Your title search will show it.

faqs.q: What month does the Russell County clerk hold the tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held before August ends, with newspaper and website notices beforehand. Ring the clerk's office, (270) 343-2125, for the exact date.

faqs.q: Is the Russell County homestead exemption automatic once I turn 65?
faqs.a: No, you have to apply. Bring proof of age or disability to the PVA. The deduction was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and most disability claims renew yearly.
